2.0.s.en: 1. The temple, the desire of all nations:

2.0.0.en: 1 In the seventh month, in the one and twentieth day of the month, came the word of the LORD by the prophet Haggai, saying, 2 "Speak now to Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua the son of Josedech, the high priest, and to the residue of the people, saying, 3 Who is left among you that saw this house in her first glory? and how do ye see it now? is it not in your eyes in comparison of it as nothing? 4 Yet now be strong, O Zerubbabel, saith the LORD; and be strong, O Joshua, son of Josedech, the high priest; and be strong, all ye people of the land, saith the LORD, and work: for I am with you, saith the LORD of hosts: 5 According to the word that I covenanted with you when ye came out of Egypt, so my spirit remaineth among you: fear ye not. 6 For thus saith the LORD of hosts; Yet once, it is a little while, and I will shake the heavens, and the earth, and the sea, and the dry land; 7 And I will shake all nations, and the desire of all nations shall come: and I will fill this house with glory, saith the LORD of hosts. 8 The silver is mine, and the gold is mine, saith the LORD of hosts. 9 The glory of this latter house shall be greater than of the former, saith the LORD of hosts: and in this place will I give peace, saith the LORD of hosts."

2.0.1.en: The second message came when the builders had begun the work about a month earlier, so it was a message of encouragement and support for them. If the previous prophecy had wounded them with rebuke, this prophecy bandages their wounds with encouraging words of divine comfort.

2.0.2.en: The date of this prophecy is "the seventh month, in the one and twentieth day of the month," that is, the seventh day of the Feast of Tabernacles, the last harvest feast of the Jewish year (see Lev 23:39-44). This feast was marked by joy and by thanksgiving sacrifices, offered on the last days of the feast more than on any other day.

2.0.3.en: It was fitting for all to be filled with joy, not only because of the feast but because of the beginning of the work on the house of the Lord, and to offer thanksgiving sacrifices to God, who was restoring to them the glory that had been taken from them. But the enemy of good cannot bear the joy and thanksgiving of the children of God, so he tried to crush them by sowing thoughts of despair through some of the elderly who had lived in the days of the old temple before it was destroyed (about seventy years earlier). These compared the old temple with the foundations of the new one and counted the work in progress as nothing before the splendor of the glory of the old. While the priests and Levites were singing with joy and sounding the trumpets for the work, these elderly men began to weep bitterly over the glory of the old temple. The situation almost became critical, and the enemy of good nearly turned the joyful work into sorrow, heaviness of heart and the crushing of souls.

2.1.0.en: Thus some of the elderly err by despising the work of the new generation, counting their works, when compared with former works, as nothing [3]. Therefore the wise man counsels us: "Say not thou, What is the cause that the former days were better than these?" (Eccl 7:10).

2.1.1.en: And in order to remove the spirit of despair, God began to support and encourage them in this way.

2.2.0.en: First: "Be strong, O Zerubbabel; be strong, O Joshua; and be strong, all ye people of the land, and work: for I am with you" [4]. It is as though He asks the governor, the priest and the people not to be occupied with comparisons between old and new, but to work with strength, being strong for the sake of "God" who dwells in their midst. May every believer not squander his energy on the many thoughts that crush people, but let his will be strengthened, let his heart be strengthened, and let all his powers be strengthened, working with all his power, sure that the Lord is with him, which is the secret of his joy and his glory!

2.3.0.en: If the purpose of the building is that the Lord may meet with them through the covenant and that they may enjoy His dwelling in their midst, then in the midst of the work He says to them: "According to the word that I covenanted with you when ye came out of Egypt, so my spirit remaineth among you: fear ye not" [5]. It is as though He says: Do not fear, for I enter into the covenant with you, and My Spirit dwells in your midst as long as you are working... and this is the true glory.

2.4.0.en: Second: "Yet once, it is a little while, and I will shake the heavens, and the earth, and the sea, and the dry land; and I will shake all nations, and the desire of all nations shall come: and I will fill this house with glory, saith the LORD of hosts" [6-7]. In the past, when He established the covenant at Mount Sinai, the Lord shook the place and the mountain smoked. Now He shakes heaven (the soul), earth (the body), the sea (the gifts) and the dry land (the energies). He breaks down the old man in order to raise up in us the new man, so that we bear his marks in our souls, and our bodies, our gifts and our energies are sanctified. With the shaking of the old nature we receive a new life, raised up and in harmony in body and soul, and we work for the sake of the Kingdom.

2.4.1.en: This shaking is the sign of the coming of "the desire of all nations," for He dwells within us in the waters of Baptism, when we are buried with Him, so that the powers of darkness are shaken and our outward man is broken down. And when He comes also at the end of the ages, nature will be shaken with power, so that the material world passes away and the Lord comes as a heavenly and eternal King.

2.4.2.en: Some translate "the desire of all nations shall come" as "the wealth of all nations shall come," meaning that the new temple is filled with splendor by the entrance of the Gentiles into the membership of the Church, offering their faith in the Savior and their zeal as the secret of spiritual wealth.

2.5.0.en: Third: "The silver is mine, and the gold is mine, saith the LORD of hosts" [8]. If the measures of glory were the abundance of gold, silver and precious stones that filled the old temple, then in the new house the Lord says: "Provide neither gold, nor silver, nor brass in your purses" (Mt 10:9), since He Himself is our silver and our gold, He is the adornment of the house and its glory.

2.5.1.en: St. John Chrysostom sees that the prophet spoke this phrase because many of the Jews found it hard to believe how the old temple could return again with its gold and silver after it had become dust and ashes. It is as though the Lord says to them: [Why do they not believe, for the silver is Mine and the gold is Mine; I do not need to borrow from anyone to adorn My house?].

2.6.0.en: Fourth: "The glory of this latter house shall be greater than of the former, saith the LORD of hosts: and in this place will I give peace, saith the LORD of hosts" [9]. If we compare the glory of the first temple, which Solomon built, with that of the latter, which Zerubbabel built, we find that the first was greater in the precious stones and gold it contained and in the magnificence of the building. It is also recorded in the Babylonian Talmud that the temple of Zerubbabel lacked five things that the temple of Solomon had: the glory of the Shekinah, the holy fire, the Ark of the Covenant, the Urim and Thummim, and the spirit of prophecy. But here He lifts us up not to the temple of Zerubbabel but to the temple to which the Lord referred as being His body (Jn 2). How glorious is the new temple in which reconciliation between the Father and mankind was accomplished through the shedding of blood (Col 1:20)! Therefore He says: "And in this place will I give peace, saith the LORD of hosts."

2.7.0.en: If God disciplined His people by captivity, so that the temple of Solomon was destroyed, it was only to bring them back to build the temple in a greater glory; thus the Lord disciplines us to grant us a better splendor, as St. John Chrysostom said [11].

2.8.s.en: 2. God seeks the temple of the heart:

2.8.0.en: 10 In the four and twentieth day of the ninth month, in the second year of Darius, came the word of the LORD by Haggai the prophet, saying, 11 "Thus saith the LORD of hosts; Ask now the priests concerning the law, saying, 12 If one bear holy flesh in the skirt of his garment, and with his skirt do touch bread, or pottage, or wine, or oil, or any meat, shall it be holy?" And the priests answered and said, "No." 13 Then said Haggai, "If one that is unclean by a dead body touch any of these, shall it be unclean?" And the priests answered and said, "It shall be unclean." 14 Then answered Haggai, and said, "So is this people, and so is this nation before me, saith the LORD; and so is every work of their hands; and that which they offer there is unclean. 15 And now, I pray you, consider from this day and upward, from before a stone was laid upon a stone in the temple of the LORD: 16 Since those days were, when one came to an heap of twenty measures, there were but ten: when one came to the pressfat for to draw out fifty vessels out of the press, there were but twenty. 17 I smote you with blasting and with mildew and with hail in all the labours of your hands; yet ye turned not to me, saith the LORD. 18 Consider now from this day and upward, from the four and twentieth day of the ninth month, even from the day that the foundation of the LORD'S temple was laid, consider it. 19 Is the seed yet in the barn? yea, as yet the vine, and the fig tree, and the pomegranate, and the olive tree, hath not brought forth: from this day will I bless you."

2.8.1.en: This prophecy came after the previous one, two months after it was declared. In it he makes clear that if the glory of the temple is the Lord's dwelling in the midst of His people, then the purpose of the temple is the sanctification of the heart. Therefore He asks us not to fix our minds on the building of stone but on the heart. For if we raise the building of stone with defiled hearts, what benefit is it? The following is to be noted in this prophecy:

2.8.2.en: First: God asks the prophet to ask the priests about the law, although he is a prophet. God had sent the prophet to urge the priests to work, yet He asks him to ask the priests for the interpretation of the law. It is as though every member of the Church works with the other in his own work, with no preference of one over the other except in respect of faithfulness in what has been entrusted to him: the prophet in prophecy and the priest in interpreting the law.

2.8.3.en: If the principal work of the priest is to interpret the law, as St. Jerome says: [Great is the work of the priesthood, to answer questions concerning the law... For in fact, deficiency in the priest's teaching hinders him from doing good to others... and as much as he builds up the Church of Christ by the virtues of his life, he harms it all the more by his failure to resist those who drag it downward.]

2.8.4.en: Second: If a man bears holy flesh in the skirt of his garment and with his skirt touches something, it does not make it holy; but if he has been defiled by a dead body, what he touches he defiles. It is as though He wanted to affirm that contagion passes to the lives of others more quickly in sin than in holiness, because demolishing is quicker than building. It is as though He asks them to care for their spiritual health and sanctification, because every sickness and uncleanness is transmitted and spreads among them quickly.

2.9.0.en: Third: He says, "If one bear holy flesh," and He did not say "a holy sacrifice." When they insist on evil, God does not accept from them the building of His house, however magnificent and beautiful it may seem, and does not accept their sacrifices but sees them as "flesh." He asks them to examine themselves, lest while they are occupied with the outward building they lose the sanctification of the heart, for He says: "And now, I pray you, consider from this day and upward, from before a stone was laid upon a stone in the temple of the LORD" [15].

2.10.0.en: Fourth: Since the heart is not sanctified, even if they build a temple for the Lord in their midst they do not enjoy the blessing, for He says: "Since those days were, when one came to an heap of twenty measures, there were but ten: when one came to the pressfat for to draw out fifty vessels out of the press, there were but twenty. I smote you with blasting and with mildew and with hail in all the labours of your hands; yet ye turned not to me, saith the LORD" [16-17]. A man comes to the threshing floor expecting to gather twenty measures of grain, and he gathers only ten; he comes to the winepress to draw out fifty vessels of the juice of the grapes and finds only twenty. As for the plants, He strikes them with blasting (the blowing of a violent wind), with mildew (pests) and with hail. Thus nature opposes him, perhaps to bring him back to his Creator.

2.11.s.en: 3. The new temple and the divine seal:

2.11.0.en: 20 And again the word of the LORD came unto Haggai in the four and twentieth day of the month, saying, 21 "Speak to Zerubbabel, governor of Judah, saying, I will shake the heavens and the earth; 22 And I will overthrow the throne of kingdoms, and I will destroy the strength of the kingdoms of the heathen; and I will overthrow the chariots, and those that ride in them; and the horses and their riders shall come down, every one by the sword of his brother. 23 In that day, saith the LORD of hosts, will I take thee, O Zerubbabel, my servant, the son of Shealtiel, saith the LORD, and will make thee as a signet: for I have chosen thee, saith the LORD of hosts."

2.11.1.en: This last prophecy was declared on the very day on which the previous prophecy was declared. In the former the Lord affirms the necessity of directing eyes to the temple of the heart and its sanctification, so that the believer may be filled with blessing and enjoy the Lord's dwelling within him; but here the speech is directed to Zerubbabel the governor, who was of the seed of David, declaring that He blesses him by breaking down the opposing pagan nations and by setting him as a signet for the Lord, as the one chosen from His heart.

2.11.2.en: If Zerubbabel represents the Lord Christ, who was "born in Babylon," in that He took our body and came to our earth and entered with us even into the tomb, yet He is the only Son, in whom the Father is well pleased, and in Him we have become God's chosen ones (Eph 1:4). In Him we enjoy victory, not over human nations with their chariots and horses, but over the evil powers of darkness.

2.11.3.en: By Baptism the works of the old man are defeated under our feet like collapsing pagan nations, and we enjoy the heavenly seal, which the bride longed for, saying: "Set me as a seal upon thine heart, as a seal upon thine arm" (Song 8:6). By it we have become like a signet, bearing the honor of the Lord, His riches and His spiritual authority, and we bear witness to Him as a bride united with Him on a transcendent level.
